title: Asia capitals three of seven · South Asia
edition: Asia capitals · Seven regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Asia capitals, episode three of seven. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Seven capitals of South Asia: the two planned capitals of the north, the Hindu Kush, the Himalaya, the Bengal delta and the island of Sri Lanka.

states.name: New Delhi
lines: New Delhi stands on the Yamuna river in north-central India, about fifteen kilometres from the older city of Delhi.
Planned by the architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker and inaugurated in 1931, its Rashtrapati Bhavan, the president's palace, has some 340 rooms.
Remember New Delhi as the planned garden capital of 1931, with India Gate for the soldiers of the First World War.
states.transition: Let's bring New Delhi into view.

states.name: Islamabad
lines: Islamabad was built in the 1960s as a new capital at the foot of the Margalla Hills, in the north of Pakistan.
Its Faisal Mosque, shaped like a desert tent, was for years the largest in the world, and its twin city Rawalpindi lies right next to it.
Remember Islamabad as the new tent-shaped mosque capital of the 1960s, beside its twin city.

states.name: Kabul
lines: Kabul lies in a valley among the mountains of the Hindu Kush, in the east of Afghanistan, at about 1,800 metres.
Babur, the founder of the Mughal empire, asked to be buried here, and his garden tomb still stands.
Remember Kabul as the high valley capital where Babur asked to be buried, and one of the highest capitals in the world.

states.name: Kathmandu
lines: Kathmandu stands in a valley north of the Himalayas, in the centre of Nepal, at about 1,400 metres.
From Kasthamandap, a temple said to have been built from the wood of a single tree, its Durbar Square belongs to the valley's UNESCO site.
Remember Kathmandu as the temple of a single tree, with the stupa of Swayambhunath on its hill.

states.name: Thimphu
lines: Thimphu lies in a valley in the north of Bhutan, on the Wang Chhu river below the mountains that ring the kingdom.
A capital without traffic lights: police officers direct the traffic by hand. It became the capital in 1961.
Remember Thimphu as the capital with no traffic lights, its police waving cars through the valley by hand.

states.name: Dhaka
lines: Dhaka stands on the Buriganga river in the centre of Bangladesh, in the delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna.
Often called the rickshaw capital of the world, it is one of the most densely populated cities in the world.
Remember Dhaka as the rickshaw capital of the delta, with Louis Kahn's parliament house of 1982.

states.name: Colombo
lines: Colombo stands on the west coast of Sri Lanka, on the shore facing the Indian Ocean; the official capital, Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, lies on its edge.
Its seaside park, Galle Face Green, dates from 1859, and Arab traders knew its harbour centuries before the Portuguese arrived in 1505.
Remember Colombo as the commercial capital on the Indian Ocean, with a harbour known to Arab traders long before the Portuguese.

recap: New Delhi and Islamabad are the twentieth-century planned capitals, with Kabul in the Hindu Kush between them. Kathmandu and Thimphu are the Himalayan valleys, Dhaka the delta, and Colombo the ocean port.

Remember the garden capital of 1931, the tent-shaped mosque, Babur's tomb, the temple of a single tree, the capital with no traffic lights, the rickshaw capital, and the harbour Arab traders knew first.
